Service's PAM context has a TTY even when it was not requested (v258 regression)

### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd-258.1-1-x86_64

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.17.1-arch1-1

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

With systemd v257.7 and earlier, PAM modules like `pam_access` were called without `PAM_TTY` being set if the corresponding service unit did not request a TTY via `StandardInput` or `TTYPath`. This allowed access rules to correctly distinguish between interactive logins and system-level user services.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

With systemd v258.1, PAM modules are called with `PAM_TTY` set (e.g., to `tty1`), even when the service unit does not request a TTY. This breaks PAM configurations that rely on the absence of a TTY to identify non-interactive sessions.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. Create user (e.g., `backup`).
2. Add the following rules to `/etc/security/access.conf`:
```Ini
# Allow root logins only on local TTYs
-:root:ALL EXCEPT LOCAL
+:root:tty1 tty2 tty3 tty4 tty5 tty6

# Restrict the backup user to specific IPs
+:backup:<IP1> <IP2>

# Allow `systemd-user` to log in as any user
+:ALL:systemd-user

# Deny the rest
-:ALL:ALL
```
3. Log in as the `backup` user via SSH from a permitted IP.

The SSH login succeeds, but the associated `user@<uid>` service fails to start in the background because of a PAM permission error.

On systemd 257.7, the `+:ALL:systemd-user` rule would correctly catch all `user@` service invocations. Because the service didn't specify a TTY to PAM, `pam_access` would fall back to checking the service name (`systemd-user`) and grant access.
On systemd v258.1, this no longer works. The logs show that `tty1` is being passed as `PAM_TTY` to the modules, causing `pam_access` to deny the request based on the user's TTY instead of the service name.
The `user@.service` unit definition still does not specify a TTY, so it feels inconsistent for one to be assigned within the PAM context.

I think this regression was introduced by PR #38522. It seems that if no `TTYPath=` is explicitly set in the service's unit definition, `exec_context_tty_path` defaults to `/dev/console`, which is then resolved to `/dev/ttyX`.

### systemd version the issue has been seen with

260.1

### Used distribution

NixOS 26.05.20260523.2991645

### Linux kernel version used

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

A timer unit configured with `RandomizedOffsetSec` and `Persistent=true` will, after missing an activation time, will trigger both when the timer unit next activates, and at the next scheduled invocation based on the `OnCalendar` and `RandomizedOffsetSec` times.

For example, consider a unit with with `OnCalendar=hourly`, `RandomizedOffsetSec=60min` and `Persistent=true`, where the random offset happens to be 55 minutes.

Normally this unit would fire at 01:55, 02:55, 03:55, …. If the timer is deactivated at 09:50, then reactivated at 10:05, it will fire as soon as it is activated thanks to the persistent setting. It should then continue with the pattern previously established, and fire again at 10:55.

Essentially, `OnCalendar=hourly` + `RandomizedOffsetSec=60min` should act as though the `OnCalendar` setting is whatever its normalised value is plus the offset, so in the example above, as if it were `OnCalendar=*:55:00` with no `RandomizedOffsetSec`.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

Context directories receive unescaping in deserialization (problematic for RuntimeDirectory=%i)

### systemd version the issue has been seen with

260

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.19.14

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86-64, arm

### Component

systemctl / systemd-executor

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Services for which the value set for `RuntimeDirectory=` contains a backslash should create a runtime directory with a backslash.

For template units, it may be desirable to give each instance their own runtime directory (cf. `systemd-journald@.service`). Escaping of instance name characters may introduce backslashes.

Given its use in filenames for installed services, I expect `systemd-escape`d instance names to be usable as directory names. I could not find anything in the documentation that suggests this is not the case, nor that some kind of backslash-escaping is performed on the value of `RuntimeDirectory=` (and possibly others).

If the current behavior is intentional, it would be nice if there were a way to still use the escaped instance name as (part of) a directory name.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw


When the value set for `RuntimeDirectory=` contains a backslash, trying to start the service results in the following `systemctl` output
```
Job for [...] failed because the control process exited with error code.
```
and the journal mentions
```
Apr 28 16:02:12 HOSTNAME systemd-executor[PID]: Failed to deserialize: Invalid argument
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

The following `demo@.service` may or may not work depending on the instance name.
```systemd.service
[Unit]
Description=Backslash shenanigans

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/printf '%%s' %f
RemainAfterExit=yes
RuntimeDirectory=demo/%i
```

With
```
systemctl start $(systemd-escape --template=demo@.service --path "$(realpath foo)")
```
everything works fine, but with
```
systemctl start $(systemd-escape --template=demo@.service --path "$(realpath foo-v1)")
```
we run into trouble as the hyphen is escaped as `\x2d`.

Note that the backslash does not need to be introduced by `%i`: a literal backslash also causes the same behavior.


### Further observations

Oddly enough, if the number of consecutive backslashes (`k`) is 3 or 4 mod 4, the path is interpreted as `⌈k/4⌉`, suggesting some form of escaping is at play.
Furthermore, given the use of `RuntimeDirectory=systemd/journal.%i` in `systemd-journald@.service`, I expect that service to be vulnerable to the current issue when given an unfortunate namespace name.


### Prevalence

The issue could also be reproduced with systemd 255 on arm (Yocto Linux scarthgap) and x86-64 (Ubuntu 24.04).
